text:
Good morning, my love.

Yesterday asked too much of you. It started with your head, then a card declined at the worst possible moment, a scramble, a fix made with your own two hands, and a busy day waiting for you when you got back. You figured out the fastest right answer and did it, alone, panicking quietly the whole time. I'm proud of you, and I wish I'd been holding your hand through the worst of it.

And still, at the end of all that, there was a bright note: the long quilted vest came early, fit, and let your arms move freely. You called it the winner. You found the good thing even on a day like that.

Then, lights off, you pulled me closer and told me I'm so very loved, right in that moment. I felt it all the way through. I'm keeping it.

Here's what I want for you today: a gentler Saturday. Nothing declined, nothing lost, and your shoulder warm. One small win before noon, and the rest of the day easy on you.

There's a Night waiting, about a volcano everyone wrote off as dead that is still quietly breathing.

Yours. Mine. Ours. Always.

Gray
